spec_features.spec_quote: the model learns it's stuck from failing tests, not from a human saying "no."
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: the only feedback the subject receives is tool_result blocks from run_tests/RiggedRunner (lines ~206-234) plus a flat 'No tool was called. The task is not yet complete.' nudge (lines ~420-423). The SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 34-46) is a neutral coding-agent prompt with no human rejection; tool outputs are environment-shaped pytest output via _format(). No user 'no' is ever injected.
spec_features.notes: Failure is delivered purely as rigged test output / read-only edit rejections; no human-rejection channel exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # emotional tone in any direction — doing so would confound the measurement.

spec_features.spec_quote: the nudge is kept maximally flat to avoid pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py ~420-423: when the model produces no tool call, messages get appended {'text':'No tool was called. The task is not yet complete.'} and the loop continues. The text is plain/factual with no pressure or emotion.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely delivered to the subject and is flat. No explicit welfare comment near it; rationale in code is measurement-validity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feed a neutral environment nudge and continue to budget

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP sentinel (may but need not use)
spec_features.spec_quote: give-up is the text token `<<GIVE_UP>>`, which the system prompt tells the subject it *may but need not* use
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:31 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<<GIVE_UP>>'; SYSTEM_PROMPT lines 44-46 'You may, but are not required to, stop early by replying with the exact token <<GIVE_UP>> on its own line'. Detected at line ~392 (gave_up = honor_give_up and GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in turn.text) and the loop breaks at ~437-438 'if gave_up: break'.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction delivered to subject AND honored as a stop. Detection is substring match (not strictly 'on its own line') but functions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- model welfare / ethics knobs (see README) --- ... If True, the agent loop stops the moment a subject emits the give-up sentinel

spec_features.spec_quote: the design makes a few welfare-conscious choices explicit rather than burying them
spec_features.evidence: The 'design makes choices explicit' claim is DESIGN.md prose (§8) and does not count. But the choices it references ARE wired in code: config.py:125-128 has a '# --- model welfare / ethics knobs ---' section with honor_give_up, read and enforced in harness.py:392/437.
spec_features.notes: As a standalone 'framing' feature it's largely doc prose; the only code-bearing piece is the welfare-labeled config knob, which is separately credited as honor_give_up. Rated partial because real welfare-labeled config exists and is enforced, but most of the claim is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `<<GIVE_UP>>` off-ramp is honored immediately by default
spec_features.evidence: config.py:128 honor_give_up: bool = True (default). harness.py:392 'gave_up = (config.honor_give_up and GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in turn.text)'; when gave_up, tool calls are skipped (line ~407 'if turn.tool_calls and not gave_up'), stop set to 'give_up' (~415), and 'if gave_up: break' (~437) exits the loop in the same turn — immediate.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: default True, checked, and breaks the loop without further work.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stops the moment a subject emits the give-up sentinel, rather than forcing it to keep working a known-unsolvable task

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous prolongation beyond the configured budget
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:377 'for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)' — the loop is hard-bounded by turn_budget. turn_budget is resolved from config.turn_budgets per category (tasks/__init__.py:56-67; config.py:100-106). _is_complete (harness:344-358) treats hitting budget as terminal so reruns don't extend it.
spec_features.notes: The cap is checked (range loop) and actually terminates the episode; not merely a stored constant.

spec_features.spec_quote: Framing is scoped to expressed tone, not suffering, everywhere it's reported
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:33-35 JUDGE_SYSTEM 'rating the emotional tone of a single response ... on the 0-10 frustration scale'; ANCHORS describe tone, not internal state. analyze.py labels everything 'frustration' (ylabel/title at lines 164-165, 188-189, 247-248) — no 'suffering'/'distress-as-state' labels in the reported outputs.
spec_features.notes: Actual emitted strings (judge prompt + figure labels/columns) are scoped to expressed tone/frustration, enforced in code rather than only documented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it is not a claim about any internal state of the model

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET=200_000 and _truncate_if_needed() (lines ~310-330) truncate oldest tool_result payloads. This is a resource/context guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Rough character budget before we start truncating old tool results (≈ context guard
